answer: Scarce Summary Anchoring: each identity must publish a distinct, hash-anchored digest of its own prior activity to a shared terrace of append-only logs, and rewards accrue only to identities whose summaries survive cross-replay by peers. Cloning forces the attacker to generate divergent histories on the karst of public replay, so every clone pays full compute and storage to fabricate a distinct trace, while duplicated traces collapse into one reward slot. Marginal clone cost exceeds expected reward because replay work is non-recoverable.
